clue.text: Craft, if moving about

indicators.note: letters moving about are shifted into a fresh order, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boat, if it is under way, is part of the flow on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: An &lit: rearranging CRAFTIF, signalled by 'moving about', gives the answer, and the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehicles or vessels in motion along a route are collectively called the flow of craft on it.

clue.text: Test case

definitions.meaning: a test or experiment to see how something performs
a court case heard before a judge

explanation.definitionFit: Both a trying-out and a hearing in court go by the same word.

clue.text: Infant (tiny) drops back a pound, which is dreadful

indicators.note: drops tells us letters are let fall from the words just built

parts.note: an infant is a baby
tiny means small
B is a standard abbreviation for back, as in a football position
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A small baby falls, losing a pound in weight, which is awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' removes B and L from BABYSMALL to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysmal is a synonym for dreadful or appallingly bad.

clue.text: London number called but not paid for

indicators.note: called means said out loud, here in a Cockney accent

parts.note: a number spoken in a London Cockney accent, where the TH sounds like F: three

explanation.surface: A London telephone number is rung, but the call is not charged.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney, the working-class London accent, TH is said as F, so 'three' comes out sounding like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given without charge costs nothing, so it is complimentary.

clue.text: It helps to keep away from tobacco

definitions.text: It helps to keep away from tobacco

parts.words: It helps to keep away from tobacco
parts.note: sounds like an aid for quitting smoking, but is a tube that keeps the smoker's fingers and lips away from the burning leaf

explanation.surface: A device that helps a smoker give up.
explanation.definitionFit: A long holder keeps a smoke held at a distance from the fingers and mouth.

clue.text: Shame about American support

indicators.note: about means placed around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: a stain is a mark of shame or disgrace

explanation.surface: A disgrace concerning American backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain is to hold up or support, as a beam bears a load.

clue.text: Welcome subject of discussion

parts.note: the phrase said when the very person being talked about turns up

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said when someone appears just as they are being mentioned.

clue.text: Beg kitty to lie about with wild pups

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as fodder

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: taken as written
a kitty is a cat

explanation.surface: Ask the cat to lie down among some boisterous puppies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kitty' sounds like a pot of money but is just a cat; 'wild' and 'about' are the two working words, the second putting one piece round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To supplicate is to plead humbly, a formal synonym for beg.

clue.text: Claims of length reflected in times

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside another

parts.note: ages are long times or eras

indicators.note: reflected means turned back as in a mirror, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: an ell is an old unit of length

explanation.surface: Claims about distance mirrored in various periods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns ELL into LLE, which goes 'in' AGES. An ell is an old cloth measure of about 45 inches.
explanation.definitionFit: Alleges as a verb means asserts or claims, usually without proof.

clue.text: No artist detailed on church register

indicators.note: de-tailed means having its tail, the last letter, removed

parts.note: Titian was the Venetian Renaissance painter

explanation.surface: No painter is recorded in the parish records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' cuts the last letter from TITIAN. Notitia is a rare word for a register of churches or ecclesiastical sees.
explanation.definitionFit: A notitia is a list or register, especially of the dioceses of a church.

clue.text: Academic union that is vaguely in order

indicators.note: putting the letters in order means arranging them afresh

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A college alliance that is vaguely well organised.
explanation.definitionFit: The group of eight elite US universities forms an athletic and academic association.

clue.text: Guide one in area of land

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside another

parts.note: a plot is a small area of land
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A guide on a plot of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot guides ships into harbour, so as a verb it means steer or guide.

clue.text: Illumination using large quantity of electricity

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
an amp is a unit of electric current

explanation.surface: Lighting that consumes a great deal of power.
explanation.definitionFit: A light fitting provides illumination, so the device stands for the light it gives.

clue.text: Frustration over lecher warns followers

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the first word is laid round the second

parts.note: a blight is something that frustrates or spoils plans
a rake is a dissolute, womanising man

explanation.surface: Disappointment about a womaniser alerts his admirers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'followers' are the drivers in the cars behind, who are warned when the car ahead slows.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear red signal tells following drivers that the car in front is slowing.

clue.text: Natty outfit displayed round ramshackle area

indicators.note: round means going around, so one word encloses another

parts.note: shown means displayed

indicators.note: to outfit is to fit out, here a fresh arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A smart outfit is exhibited around a run-down district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Natty outfit' reads as smart clothing, but 'outfit' signals a rearrangement, and 'round' wraps the synonym for displayed around the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A district of makeshift shacks is a slum, a ramshackle area of a city.

clue.text: Told that beheadings are things of the past

indicators.note: beheadings means each word loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: the head, first letter, of the word told
the head, first letter, of the word that
the head, first letter, of the word told
the head, first letter, of the word that

explanation.surface: Someone is told that executions belong to history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheadings' takes the first letter T from each of TOLD and THAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of date or no longer novel is said to be passé, belonging to the past.

clue.text: Plant confusingly spoken of for some time to come?

indicators.note: confusingly spoken means said in a garbled way, so one word comes out like another

parts.note: the future is the time still to come

explanation.surface: A plant mumbled about as something for years ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The flower, said 'FEW-sha', can be mispronounced to sound like a slurred 'future'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuchsia is a shrub with drooping red and purple flowers, named after Leonhart Fuchs.

clue.text: Permit to break silence

indicators.note: to break the word is to smash it and reassemble its pieces

explanation.surface: Permission to speak up.
explanation.definitionFit: To license something is to authorise or permit it officially.

clue.text: What moved Marx to wreck film set?

indicators.note: to wreck the words is to break them up into a new order

explanation.surface: What drove Marx to destroy a movie set?
explanation.walkthrough: 'to wreck' rearranges FILMSET. The surface suggests the Marx Brothers on a film set; it is Karl Marx.
explanation.definitionFit: Left-wing politics, the ideology Marx championed, is called leftism.

clue.text: Mythical horseman

parts.note: not a rider but a man who is half horse in Greek legend

explanation.definitionFit: This creature of Greek myth has a man's head and torso on a horse's body.

clue.text: Hang-up about direction of rocket science

indicators.note: about means placed around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: a hitch is a snag or hang-up
E is east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A problem concerning the course of space engineering.
explanation.definitionFit: Advanced technology is the kind of field loosely called rocket science.

clue.text: Concerts start with one Ravel composition for keyboard instrument

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
a composition is a putting together, here the letters arranged anew

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Concerts open with a Ravel piece for the keyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' rearranges I and RAVEL to LAVIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A clavier is any keyboard instrument, such as a harpsichord or clavichord.

clue.text: Imagine in idols nothing but frippery …

parts.note: to fancy is to imagine

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside another

parts.note: idols are false gods
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Picture nothing but trivial ornaments among idols.
explanation.definitionFit: Frippery means showy, trivial ornaments, the trinkets sold as decorative novelties.

clue.text: … becoming reasonable

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both handsome in appearance and just or moderate.

clue.text: Uncommon, like Tunbridge Wells

definitions.meaning: not a commoner, being of the king's family
Tunbridge Wells, a Kent spa town

explanation.definitionFit: Members of the monarch's family are not commoners, and the Kent town bears that royal title.

clue.text: 16 down proponent with wrong standing

indicators.note: standing in a down clue means set upright, read from the bottom up

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A supporter with a bad position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' turns TORT upward. A Trot is a Trotskyist, a hard-left supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trot, short for Trotskyist, is a proponent of left-wing views.

clue.text: Gordius is past a perfect state

parts.note: the setter Gordius says of himself 'I am', I'm
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: The setter claims to be beyond perfection.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is the final, perfect adult stage of an insect.

clue.text: Is this a 27 meaning of "Oxbridge"?

parts.note: Oxbridge combines two universities; read word for word, a word starting with the prefix for two and ending like varsity describes it

explanation.walkthrough: 27 is LITERAL. Oxbridge is Oxford plus Cambridge, two varsities; DI means two.
explanation.definitionFit: Variety and difference is what the word means, but the cryptic reading is two universities.

clue.text: Seafarer — Eliot's character includes one

indicators.note: includes means the first piece holds the second within it

parts.note: Silas Marner is the title character of George Eliot's novel
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sailor in George Eliot's novel features a single person.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariner is a sailor, one who travels by sea.

clue.text: Misprint could be a tiller

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might form something else if rearranged

explanation.surface: A typo may turn into a boat's steering handle.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, a literal is a typographical error, a misprint of a letter.
